module_title: Data Privacy, Compliance & Governance (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS)
description: Master data regulatory architecture: GDPR Right to be Forgotten in immutable append-only logs, Crypto-Shredding, PCI-DSS Tokenization Vaults, and HIPAA PII / PHI Encryption.

topics.title: GDPR Compliance in Immutable Systems: Crypto-Shredding & Anonymization
topics.definition: GDPR Article 17 mandates the 'Right to be Forgotten' (erasing user personal data on request). In immutable systems (Apache Kafka, Event Sourcing, WORM storage), records cannot be deleted. Crypto-Shredding solves this by encrypting each user's PII with a unique per-user encryption key and destroying the key upon deletion request.
topics.why_we_need_it: Rewriting multi-terabyte Kafka logs or S3 backups to delete 1 user's email corrupts log offsets and takes hours of compute. Crypto-shredding makes data permanently unreadable in 1 millisecond.
topics.real_world_analogy: Locking your diary in a steel safe with a unique key: if you throw the key into a volcano (Crypto-Shredding), the diary is still physically in the room, but no one on Earth can ever read it again.
topics.how_it_works:
1. Per-User Key Management: When User 123 registers, generate a unique AES-256 Data Encryption Key (DEK) managed in AWS KMS / HashiCorp Vault.
2. Field-Level Encryption: Encrypt all PII fields (Name, Email, SSN, Address) using `DEK_123` before writing to Kafka or PostgreSQL.
3. Crypto-Shredding (Erasure Request): When User 123 requests account deletion under GDPR, delete `DEK_123` from the Key Vault. All historical Kafka events, S3 backups, and DB records encrypted with that key become permanently unrecoverable random noise, satisfying legal erasure requirements without modifying append-only logs.
